winning_case.argument: Tatum, because when you need somebody to run the offense, you take the creator.

royce.claim: Jaylen Brown is better right now: he has the Finals MVP, the steadier availability, and the cleaner scoring.
supports: Honors: Finals MVP in 2024 and 5 All-Star selections (F11, F12)
Availability: 71 of 82 last season against Tatum's 16 (F7, F3)
Rate stat: Brown's true shooting beats Tatum's this season, plus 6.9 boards to 6.0 (F16, F15, F18, F17)
royce.answer: To the point that Tatum has more All-Star picks and more assists, he concedes the 6-to-5 and says assists come in a small sample and honors are the past, while Brown's Finals MVP was won on the biggest stage.

deacon.claim: Tatum is better right now: he scores more and creates far more for teammates, at a small efficiency cost.
supports: Honors over time: 6 All-Star selections to 5 (F9, F12)
deacon.answer: He grants Brown's better true shooting (F15, F16) and the small samples, then shows the gap is small next to the five extra points and four extra assists a night.

lonnie.claim: Tatum is the better player right now because of his role: he runs the offense and creates, which is the job a team can't replace.
supports: Role: 7.9 assists a night as the Celtics' creator (F19, F20)
Shared title: the same 2024 championship, so the ring doesn't separate them (F8, F10)
Availability: back and playing 7 of 8 this season, 23 games since the Achilles (F21, F4, F3)
lonnie.answer: Granting that the Achilles is a fair question, he points to 7 of 8 games played this season and says last season's 16 answers a different question than 'right now'.

beats: Opening positions: Royce for Brown on the Finals MVP, Lonnie and Deacon for Tatum on creation and scoring
Clash over efficiency and availability: Deacon concedes true shooting, Royce brings 71 vs 16 games, Lonnie says that's last season
The trap: Royce's honors standard turns against him (6 All-Stars to 5), then Lonnie's 7-game assist sample gets turned on him
Decisive exchange: Royce catches the small sample, Deacon concedes it and names what would flip him

lines.speaker: hal
lines.text: You're on the Sideline. Go ahead, Dana from Scranton.

lines.speaker: caller
lines.text: My brother and I have argued about this since Sunday dinner. Jayson Tatum or Jaylen Brown, who's better right now? Loser buys the wings.

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: Brown. He's the Finals MVP, 2024, and he's a five-time All-Star. He plays like a freight train that learned to shoot threes. And he was on the floor for 71 of 82 games last season. That's the guy you want.

stat.label: Jaylen Brown · NBA Finals MVP
stat.definition: From his Wikipedia page: NBA Finals MVP (2024)

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: Same ring, though. Tatum won that title too. And you said right now, Royce. This season Tatum's handing out 7.9 assists a night to Brown's 3.9. To my eye, the Celtics' offense runs through him. So who's creating for everybody else on the other side?

stat.label: Jayson Tatum · NBA champion
stat.definition: From his Wikipedia page: NBA champion (2024)

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: Listen, Lonnie's right, and scoring says the same: 27.0 to 21.8. Now, Brown's the more efficient scorer, 56.8 true shooting to 55.1. That's scoring efficiency counting threes and free throws. I'll give him that. But that's a small efficiency edge for a big gap in scoring. And it's seven, eight games. I'd hold all of it loosely.

stat.label: Jayson Tatum · points per game
stat.definition: Points scored per game, on average.

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: You just gave me the efficiency, Deacon. That gap in scoring is just more shots. And Tatum played 16 games last season. You can't build the best player on a guy you're waiting on.

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: Fair question after an Achilles. I'd want to see the burst myself. But it's last season's number, Royce. This season he's played 7 of 8, and he's got 23 games in since the injury. That's what right now looks like.

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: Right. Last season's games tell you about last season.

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: Then give me the stage. Name what Tatum did that beats Finals MVP.

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: You want honors voted on over years? Six All-Star selections to five. That's Tatum.

stat.label: Jayson Tatum · NBA All-Star selection
stat.definition: From his Wikipedia page: 6× NBA All-Star (2020–2025)

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: Right, six to five. That's the trophy case, Deacon, not tonight. And tonight Brown's pulling down 6.9 boards to his 6.0, and still scoring cleaner. That's the more complete night.

stat.label: Jaylen Brown · rebounds per game
stat.definition: Rebounds grabbed per game, on average.

lines.speaker: hal
lines.text: We've had honors and games played. What does an actual possession look like for each of them?

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: Brown does things Tatum doesn't, the threes, the steals, to my read. But 27 and nearly eight assists? That's the one line the team can't replace. If Tatum's out of the lineup, who creates?

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: Seven games, Lonnie. Deacon just told you not to bet on eight. And you're building on seven.

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: Okay, that's fair, mine too. If those assists hold up once he's played a lot more games, I'm right. If they drop to Brown's level, I'm wrong, and I'll say it right here.

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: Notice what he didn't say. Brown's got the trophy that settles who showed up when it counted. Remember that.

lines.speaker: hal
lines.text: Final answers. One sentence each.

lines.speaker: royce
lines.text: Brown, because the best player is the one who owns the biggest stage, and he's the Finals MVP.

lines.speaker: deacon
lines.text: Tatum, because a guy who scores that much and sets up that many teammates is giving you two kinds of value.

lines.speaker: lonnie
lines.text: Tatum, because when you need somebody to run the offense, you take the creator.

lines.speaker: hal
lines.text: On the scorecard, tonight goes to Lonnie. His case was about who creates for the team right now, and Tatum is handing out 7.9 assists a night to Brown's 3.9.

lines.speaker: hal
lines.text: That's the board. Thanks for the call, Dana.
